The '''Duinuogwuin''', colloquially called '''Star Dragons''', were among [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] more secretive and strange [[Species/Legends|species]].

==Biology and appearance==
Though variable in appearance, Duinuogwuin generally had serpentine bodies, diaphanous wings, and a pair of [[Limb/Legends|legs]] on each of many body segments. The legs on their frontmost segment were used as arms with fully articulated hands. Their average length was ten [[Meter/Legends|meters]], but some were rumored to be one hundred meters or more. Duinuogwuin were covered in scales which ranged from various shades of gray or pale blue to black in [[Color/Legends|color]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" />

[[File:Duinuogwuin-GatORW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Duinuogwuin host]]
Aside from guesswork based on observations of live Duinuogwuin, little is known of their biology, as they never gave up their bodies to scientific research. Instead, they went to an uncharted planet in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] known as "[[The Graveyard of the Dragons]]" to die. It was believed that they had internal organs which acted as [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]], since their wings were too delicate for such large creatures to take off from any but the lowest [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] planets. Some Star Dragons had the ability to exhale superheated gases, leading to speculation that they also had internal organs capable of organic cold fusion. One of their most impressive abilities was the ability to fly and survive in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of deep [[Realspace/Legends|space]] for [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] or [[Standard month/Legends|months]] at a [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /> Duinuogwuin could also live as long as 6,000 [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]].<ref name="GORW" /> Their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] was unknown, or at least unrevealed by the Star Dragons. Individual Duinuogwuin had been seen on such far-scattered [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] as [[Cona/Legends|Cona]], [[Iego/Legends|Iego]], [[Barab I/Legends|Barab I]], [[Columus/Legends|Columus]], and [[Arkania]]. They had even been sighted in deep space far from any planet.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /><ref name="GORW" />

It was known that when two Star Dragons did [[Reproduction/Legends|mate]], there was a good chance that they would produce unintelligent offspring, little more than ravening monsters. Such creatures would usually have to be [[Death/Legends|destroyed]] by their [[Parent/Legends|parents]]. Others showed intelligence, but only in the form of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|evil]] cunning. Given the likelihood of having to destroy their own offspring if they mated, most Duinuogwuin lived in isolation from others of their kind. This might have been due to their highly variable genetic code&mdash;hatchlings could emerge with genetic adaptations which were not hinted at by their ancestors. Their variable genetics may have led to completely separate [[Species/Legends|species]] to be descended from the Duinuogwuin. [[Krayt dragon/Legends|Krayt dragons]] were believed by some to be the descendants of an accidental concentration of unintelligent Duinuogwuin offspring on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /> Another sentient species, the [[Kadri'Ra]], were possible relatives of the Duinuogwuin.<ref name="Alien Encounters">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref>

==Duinuogwuin in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Then, we're not on any known world?''"<br />"''Princess, this is the kind of sector listed on most star-charts under the heading, 'here be space-dragons!'|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], after crash-landing on the [[Keeper's World]]|<ref name="Dread Discovery!">{{StoryCite|story=Dread Discovery!|book=Pizzazz 3}}</ref>}}
[[File:Cuddly_Duinuogwuin_OE_Color_Scan.png|thumb|right|250px|The Duinuogwuin [[Star Wing]] encountering the [[Wayfarer (Mu-2 long range shuttle)|''Wayfarer'']] in the [[Kidron system/Legends|Kidron system]]]]

The Duinuogwuin had a reputation for being wise and mysterious, helped by their very long lifespan and their indifference to questions about their past or their physiology. They were generally calm and even-tempered, and often preoccupied with cosmic musings. They were also noted for a strong, innate sense of morality. While they were friendly and gregarious with other races, the minority of aberrant Star Dragons sought only to manipulate and destroy others.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" />

Their part in the [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|history of the galaxy]] was uncertain: though clearly an ancient civilization, many of the stories were more mythological than historical. Star Dragons featured in the legends of many species, usually appearing as heroes coming to the aid of an oppressed people.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 4" /> However, many of these myths were contradictory, making it difficult to use them to learn details of Duinuogwuin history and origins.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook">''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''</ref>

In [[15,500 BBY]], the Star Dragons made first contact with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Unfortunately, it proved disastrous and sparked the [[Duinuogwuin Contention]], which saw [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] assaulted by the Star Dragons. This conflict was ended in a peace negotiated by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Fillorean]] and Duinuogwuin philosopher [[Borz'Mat'oh]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

Prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Jorus C'baoth]] and [[Tra's M'ins]] mediated a [[Duinuogwuin–Gotal conflict|conflict]] between the Duinuogwuin and the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]].<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>

At least two Duinuogwuin are known to have served the Republic as [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]: [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Willm Lywin]] who in [[4600 BBY]] founded the [[Teyan Praxeum]] on [[Teya IV]],<ref name="Star Wars Adventure Journal 11">{{JournalCite|11|The Most Dangerous Foe}}</ref> and a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] named [[Zephata'ru'tor]], who was killed during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]].<ref name="Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous">{{InsiderCite|86|Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous}}</ref>

Despite their historically strong moral sense, the Duinuogwuin stayed in isolation during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. They denied the fact that approximately one third of Duinuogwuin were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] in order to avoid persecution by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Rumors about the Duinuogwuin who had served as Jedi in the past were impossible to confirm during the Imperial era, due to the destruction of much of the Order's records during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]]. As late as the [[Thrawn campaign]], it was speculated that the Star Dragons were waiting to see how the conflict would be resolved before rejoining the galactic community.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" />

==Behind the scenes==
There is an inconsistency in the few visual depictions of Duinuogwuin regarding their wings. [[Operation: Elrood (book)|''Operation: Elrood'']], ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', and the cover of "[[The Most Dangerous Foe]]" all portray them with a single pair of large membranous, bat-like wings, while an illustration in ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' features several pairs of smaller, more insectoid wings.
